# MCP tools, resources and plain words

## Tools

### `site_context`

Start here. On a token of several sites, without `siteId`: its `sites`, to choose one. Otherwise the site: `guide` (how to work here, with recipes), its pages, languages, themes, components and what is live, what your role may do (`user.may`), `baseRevisions` (every leaf path at its revision, the base of a batch), `urls` (the links to hand a person: the admin, every place by its key in `places`, a page in the editor and as its draft, the live site per language; never build them yourself) and `resources` (every resource URI, ready for read_resources). A token of several sites names the site on every call with `siteId`; each answer names the site it worked on in `site`: check it before going on. Example: {}

Hints: readOnlyHint: true.

| Argument | Type | Required | Says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `siteId` | string (min 1, max 64) |  | The site, one of the ids site_context lists; a one-site token may leave it out. |

### `discover_operations`

Find what you can do: the site's ops and doors, by a plain word ("translate", "upload", "publish", "hide", "menu", "redirect", "animate") or a name prefix with a dot ("tree."). Each comes in one line: `name`, `summary`, `class` and `who` may run it, `allowed` (with `reason` when not), `undoable` (one undo in History takes it back), `dryRun` (dry_run_ops judges it), `confirm` (the confirmation it needs), `alone` (a door, alone in its batch) and one `example` input. Name ops in `names` (or pass `schemas: true`) for the whole description, every example and the input schema. What only a person does is listed too, not allowed, with the place a person does it (`place`). A token of several sites names the site on every call with `siteId`; each answer names the site it worked on in `site`: check it before going on. Example: {"query":"translate"}

Hints: readOnlyHint: true.

| Argument | Type | Required | Says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `siteId` | string (min 1, max 64) |  | The site, one of the ids site_context lists; a one-site token may leave it out. |
| `query` | string (max 200) |  | A plain word or a few ("translate", "upload", "hide", "menu", "redirect", "animate"), or a name prefix with a dot ("tree.", "page."). Empty: everything. |
| `names` | string (min 1)[] (≤20) |  | Exact names: each with its whole description, examples and input schema. |
| `schemas` | boolean |  | Every listed op with its whole description, examples and input schema. |
| `outputSchemas` | boolean |  | Add a door's output schema where it has one. |
| `cursor` | integer ≥0 |  |  |
| `limit` | integer ≥1 ≤100 |  |  |

### `read_resources`

Read up to 16 resources, each the full `libretto://site/<siteId>/<path>`: the admin's own reads, as the admin shows them, narrowed to what your role may do. The paths: `site`, `pages`, `page/<pageId>`, `node/<pageId>?node=<nodeId>`, `texts/<pageId>?lang=<locale>`, `part-settings/<pageId>?node=<nodeId>`, `style/<pageId>?node=<nodeId>`, `part/<pageId>?node=<nodeId>&revision=<revision>&entry=<entryId>&into=<pageId>`, `page-layout/<pageId>`, `seo/<pageId>`, `contrast/<pageId>`, `findings/<pageId>?locale=<locale>`, `site-findings`, `motion/<pageId>`, `definition/<key>`, `translations/<locale>?page=<pageId>`, `tokens`, `tokens/<theme>`, `design`, `design-export`, `sections`, `navigation`, `settings`, `redirects`, `media`, `media-uses/<mediaId>`, `media-space`, `forms`, `data`, `item-history/<collectionId>?item=<itemId>`, `member-roles`, `pickers`, `history`, `versions`, `version-changes/<version>`, `version-pages/<version>`, `page-restore/<version>?page=<pageId>`, `glance`, `reports`. A key in `<>` is an id from site_context or another read; other keys go in the query (`node/<pageId>?node=<nodeId>`, `node/<pageId>?node=<nodeId>&owner=layout&component=<key>` for a header, footer or layout part). One answer holds at most 40,000 characters: a long list is cut and named in `bounded` with its `next` URI (`list`, `offset`, `limit` page it), and the resources past the budget come back in `deferred` to read in another call. `reports` holds the issues you reported with report_issue and the owner's answers. Example: {"uris":["libretto://site/<siteId>/texts/87c82653-80cd-4b17-ae54-aca941cbf8a2?lang=en","libretto://site/<siteId>/navigation"]}

Hints: readOnlyHint: true.

| Argument | Type | Required | Says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `uris` | string (min 1, max 2048)[] (≤16) | yes | Full resource URIs, `libretto://site/<siteId>/<path>`, at most 16. |

### `apply_ops`

Apply one batch to the site: read before you write, and send the base revisions you read. The arguments are the batch itself, at the top level: `requestId` (a fresh UUID), `baseRevisions` (the revision of every leaf path the batch writes, from site_context.baseRevisions or your last write's `revisions`), `operations` (1 to 100 `{ name, input }`, core ops or one door), with `confirmed` and `message` when needed. Ops commit together as one step a person can undo in History, or not at all. A door (publish, rollback, undo, an upload, members, domains, mail, form messages, a site) runs alone in its batch. Styles: tree.set_style { at, node, scope, declarations } names when a value holds with a scope key: `base`, `bp:md` (from that breakpoint up), `mq:(max-width: 767.98px)`, `s:hover` (its own state), `a:hover` (an ancestor's), `pg:menu=open` (a page state), `p:<part>`, `t:<selector>` (descendants), `th:<theme>`, joined by `|` (`bp:md|s:hover`); discover_operations with names ["tree.set_style"] gives the whole grammar. A part of the header, the footer or a layout is written inside component.edit { key, ops }. Uploads travel in the call: media.uploadFile, font.uploadFace with the file as base64 in `data` (at most 20 MB; larger files and archives are a person's, in Admin › Media). Publish (publication.publish) only on the human's go, alone, confirmed ["publish"]. A write answers `ok`, `revision`, `entryId` (the step), `outputs` (what each op answered, in order: the id of what it made), `revisions` (each leaf path it wrote at its new revision: the base of your next batch), `findings` and `corrections` (what the contrast check fixed in the same step), and `undo`, the call that takes the step back while it is the newest (send it alone in apply_ops). A door answers its own result (a publish its `version`, an upload the file's `id`). A refusal says why in `message` and, where a person can do it, who (`reason`) and where: `place`, with its link `href` (site_context.urls.places). The codes: stale_revision (read again, rebuild the batch with the new revisions), operation_forbidden (your role or any agent may not: the sentence says who can; what only a person does says where), operation_not_on_core (a name of the old engine, with the op or door to use), operation_unknown (no op of this site), a core op's own code with `paths` and `opIndex`. A token of several sites names the site on every call with `siteId`; each answer names the site it worked on in `site`: check it before going on. Example: {"requestId":"0b7c6d5e-4f3a-4b2c-8d1e-9f0a1b2c3d4e","baseRevisions":{"content/87c82653-80cd-4b17-ae54-aca941cbf8a2":41},"message":"Rewrote the opening headline","operations":[{"name":"tree.set_text","input":{"at":{"page":"87c82653-80cd-4b17-ae54-aca941cbf8a2"},"node":"title001","text":"Diamo forma alla luce"}},{"name":"translation.set","input":{"at":{"page":"87c82653-80cd-4b17-ae54-aca941cbf8a2"},"locale":"en","pointer":"/tree/nodes/title001/text","value":"We give shape to light"}}]}

Hints: readOnlyHint: false, destructiveHint: true, idempotentHint: true.

| Argument | Type | Required | Says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `siteId` | string (min 1, max 64) |  | The site, one of the ids site_context lists; a one-site token may leave it out. |
| `format` | "libretto.batch" |  |  |
| `v` | 1 |  |  |
| `requestId` | uuid | yes | A fresh UUID per batch: the same requestId again answers the batch stored the first time, so a retry never writes twice. |
| `baseRevisions` | Record<string, integer ≥0> | yes | The revision of every leaf path the batch writes, as read (`content/<pageId>`, `designSystem/tokens/core`, `navigation`, ...): copy site_context.baseRevisions, or the `revisions` of your last write. A path that moved since is refused as stale_revision with the paths. |
| `operations` | ({ name: string (min 1, max 100), input: string \| number \| boolean \| null \| (string \| number \| boolean \| null \| …[] \| Record<string, …>)[] \| Record<string, string \| number \| boolean \| null \| …[] \| Record<string, …>> })[] (≤100) | yes | The calls, in order; they commit together as one step, or not at all. |

### `dry_run_ops`

Judge a batch exactly as apply_ops would, storing nothing: the same refusals, findings and contrast corrections. Worth it before a publish, a site-wide change (site.setMainLocale answers how many texts are left untranslated), an import (item.import names the bad cells) or an upload (the file checked against the site's quota); an ordinary edit can go straight to apply_ops, which writes nothing when it refuses. A door whose discovery line says `dryRun: false` (an email that goes at once, a domain) is refused here. The arguments are the batch itself, at the top level: `requestId` (a fresh UUID), `baseRevisions` (the revision of every leaf path the batch writes, from site_context.baseRevisions or your last write's `revisions`), `operations` (1 to 100 `{ name, input }`, core ops or one door), with `confirmed` and `message` when needed. Ops commit together as one step a person can undo in History, or not at all. A door (publish, rollback, undo, an upload, members, domains, mail, form messages, a site) runs alone in its batch. Styles: tree.set_style { at, node, scope, declarations } names when a value holds with a scope key: `base`, `bp:md` (from that breakpoint up), `mq:(max-width: 767.98px)`, `s:hover` (its own state), `a:hover` (an ancestor's), `pg:menu=open` (a page state), `p:<part>`, `t:<selector>` (descendants), `th:<theme>`, joined by `|` (`bp:md|s:hover`); discover_operations with names ["tree.set_style"] gives the whole grammar. A part of the header, the footer or a layout is written inside component.edit { key, ops }. A refusal says why in `message` and, where a person can do it, who (`reason`) and where: `place`, with its link `href` (site_context.urls.places). The codes: stale_revision (read again, rebuild the batch with the new revisions), operation_forbidden (your role or any agent may not: the sentence says who can; what only a person does says where), operation_not_on_core (a name of the old engine, with the op or door to use), operation_unknown (no op of this site), a core op's own code with `paths` and `opIndex`. A token of several sites names the site on every call with `siteId`; each answer names the site it worked on in `site`: check it before going on. Example: {"requestId":"0b7c6d5e-4f3a-4b2c-8d1e-9f0a1b2c3d4e","baseRevisions":{},"message":"Made English the main language","operations":[{"name":"site.setMainLocale","input":{"locale":"en"}}]}

### `render_preview`

See a page as a screenshot (a JPEG): its draft as it will be once published (default), or with target "live" the page a visitor gets now (`liveVersion` names the version). Choose the device (desktop 1440, tablet 820, mobile 390 px) or a `width` of your own, a language, a light or dark browser, the whole page, the first screen (area "viewport") or one part (crop { nodeId }), and `scroll` to capture the screen further down with motion allowed. On the draft, as the admin's View draft does: `theme` draws it under one of the site's themes, `as` as a guest, a signed-in member or a member of a role (a page for members shows its sign-in), `item` one item of a collection page. Not offered: a render document or an outline (read page/<pageId> and texts/<pageId>), a live page under a theme or as a member (the live site shows what a guest sees), a page before a batch (apply it, look, undo it). Captures share the server's few capture slots, first come, first served: `queuedMs` says how long the call waited. Its own work is bounded by 30000 ms (past it render_timeout); a queue too long (a wait past 180000 ms) answers render_busy (503) with retryAfter, the seconds to wait. A token of several sites names the site on every call with `siteId`; each answer names the site it worked on in `site`: check it before going on. Example: {"pageId":"87c82653-80cd-4b17-ae54-aca941cbf8a2","device":"mobile","locale":"en","as":"guest"}

Hints: readOnlyHint: true.

|---|---|---|---|

| `pageId` | string (min 1, max 100) | yes | The page, by its id (site_context.pages). |
| `target` | "draft" \| "live" |  | `draft` (default): the draft as it will be once published; `live`: the page as a visitor gets it now, from the version that is live. |
| `mode` | "screenshot" |  | Always a screenshot (a JPEG). |

| `locale` | string (min 2, max 35) |  | One of the site's languages (site_context.locales); absent: the main one. |

### `compare_reference`

Compare a screenshot of a draft page (as render_preview takes it) with a reference: an image of the media library (referenceMediaId), a public https image (referenceUrl, fetched once, not stored) or a public https page (referencePageUrl, captured at the same device; referenceSelector crops it to one element). The answer: `ratio` (the share of pixels that differ), `heightMismatch` and a verdict. Compare one section at a time: crop { nodeId } against the same section's referenceSelector. Every request of a reference page goes through the server's fence: https and public addresses only. Captures share the server's few capture slots, first come, first served: `queuedMs` says how long the call waited. Its own work is bounded by 30000 ms (past it render_timeout); a queue too long (a wait past 180000 ms) answers render_busy (503) with retryAfter, the seconds to wait. A token of several sites names the site on every call with `siteId`; each answer names the site it worked on in `site`: check it before going on. Example: {"pageId":"87c82653-80cd-4b17-ae54-aca941cbf8a2","device":"mobile","crop":{"nodeId":"<section id>"},"referencePageUrl":"https://example.com/about","referenceSelector":"main > section:nth-of-type(2)"}

### `report_issue`

Tell the platform owner when Libretto stops you or the person you work for: a missing door or op (category "missing-capability"), a bug, a refusal that looks wrong ("refusal"), words that mislead ("docs"). A one-line title and a Markdown body (what you were doing, for whom, what blocked you); add steps, expected and actual (the code and message), the requestId and the pageId when you have them; severity "blocking" when the person cannot go on. It changes nothing on the site. Read your reports and the owner's answers later in the `reports` resource; the person sees them in Account › Reports. At most 20 an hour per person. A token of several sites names the site on every call with `siteId`; each answer names the site it worked on in `site`: check it before going on. Example: {"title":"No door to schedule a publish","body":"The person asked to publish the spring page on Monday at 9; discover_operations finds publication.publish only, which goes live at once.","category":"missing-capability","severity":"medium"}

Hints: readOnlyHint: false, destructiveHint: false, idempotentHint: false.

| `title` | string (min 1, max 160) | yes |  |
| `body` | string (min 1, max 20000) | yes |  |
| `category` | "bug" \| "missing-capability" \| "refusal" \| "docs" \| "other" | yes |  |
| `severity` | "low" \| "medium" \| "high" \| "blocking" |  |  |
| `pageId` | string (min 1, max 36) |  |  |

## Resources

Each URI is `libretto://site/<siteId>/<path>`; `site_context.resources` lists every one, ready for `read_resources`. A key in `<>` is an id from `site_context` or another read; one answer holds at most 40,000 characters (a long list is cut and named in `bounded`, with its `next` URI).

| Path | Holds |
|---|---|
| `site` | The site: its pages, languages, themes, components, what is live, who reads and what they may do. |
| `pages` | Every page with its address, parent, layout and status, as Admin › Pages lists them. |
| `page/<pageId>` | A page: its record and its outline, one line per part. |
| `node/<pageId>?node=<nodeId>` | One part with its props and styles and the ops that write it; `owner=layout&component=<key>` reads a part of the header, footer or layout. |
| `texts/<pageId>?lang=<locale>` | A page's texts and pictures by section, in every language (`lang`: one), with the op that writes each. |
| `part-settings/<pageId>?node=<nodeId>` | A part's own settings: attributes, anchor, a code part's config, its repeat or table, an instance's overrides (`detach=1`: its Detach plan). |
| `style/<pageId>?node=<nodeId>` | Where each style value of a part comes from: its component, its site styles, its theme. |
| `part/<pageId>?node=<nodeId>&revision=<revision>&entry=<entryId>&into=<pageId>` | A part as it was at a revision, copied for another page: what a paste inserts. |
| `page-layout/<pageId>` | A page's own layout settings: the layout's variant and props, the header and footer shown or hidden, their words on this page. |
| `seo/<pageId>` | A page's search and sharing settings, in each language. |
| `contrast/<pageId>` | A page's text and ground colour pairs and how readable each is. |
| `findings/<pageId>?locale=<locale>` | What Checks finds on a page: a picture with no words, a link that says nothing, the main heading, a required value missing. |
| `site-findings` | How many findings each page of the site has. |
| `motion/<pageId>` | A page's timelines, tracks and triggers, and the motion recipes to apply. |
| `definition/<key>` | A component: its props, variants, cells, slots and parts. |
| `translations/<locale>?page=<pageId>` | The word fields in a language: of a page and the components, or of the whole site with no page. |
| `tokens` | The design tokens, or as theme `<theme>` sets them. |
| `tokens/<theme>` | The design tokens, or as theme `<theme>` sets them. |
| `design` | The design system as Design lists it: themes, token sets, fonts with what uses each, styles, breakpoints. |
| `design-export` | The design system as DTCG files (Tokens Studio's layout). |
| `sections` | What can be added: the section kinds, the saved presets and the sections of every page to copy. |
| `navigation` | The menus and their links, and what a link may point to. |
| `settings` | General values, languages, search defaults, the not-found page, integrations. |
| `redirects` | The redirects. |
| `media` | The media library: files with their words and uses, and the folders. |
| `media-uses/<mediaId>` | Where a file is used, place by place. |
| `media-space` | The bytes the site's files take and the most they may. |
| `forms` | The forms with their fields, settings and the places that use them. |
| `data` | The collections with their fields and items. |
| `item-history/<collectionId>?item=<itemId>` | One item's steps, newest first, each with the op that brings the item back as it left it. |
| `member-roles` | The member roles and the pages each opens. |
| `pickers` | Pages, files and items to pick from, by id and label. |
| `history` | The steps, newest first: who, when, what they did; a deleted page with the ops that bring it back. |
| `versions` | The saved versions and which one is live. |
| `version-changes/<version>` | What making a version live would change. |
| `version-pages/<version>` | The pages a version holds and what bringing each back would do. |
| `page-restore/<version>?page=<pageId>` | One page of a version as it would come back, with the ops that bring it back as one step. |
| `glance` | The site at a glance: what is live, the changes to publish, the last step. |
| `reports` | The issues you reported on this site with report_issue, newest first, each with its status and the platform owner's close note (`?status=open\|triaged\|closed`: one status). |

## Plain words

`discover_operations` with one of these words lists these names first (a name ending in a dot lists every name it starts).

| Word | Names |
|---|---|
| translate | `translation.set`, `site.setLocales`, `site.setMainLocale` |
